title: Visual and motor skills development in preterm and full-term infants: A protocol for longitudinal data collection
author: Ferreira, Nunes, et al.

steps.title: Identify and recruit eligible infants
steps.instruction: Recruit preterm infants (≤32 weeks gestational age) at Dr. Alfredo da Costa Maternity Hospital and full‑term infants (≥38 weeks gestational age) at Baixa Family Health Unit; confirm infants are 4 months old (corrected age for preterms) at the initial assessment; ensure parents are fluent in Portuguese or English; exclude any infant with major neurological lesions (grade III periventricular haemorrhage and/or leukomalacia), developmental disorder, congenital anomalies, congenital infections, chromosomal abnormalities, ROP with plus disease, or any other condition affecting typical development, and exclude families not planning to complete follow‑up at the study sites.

steps.title: Obtain informed consent
steps.instruction: At the 2‑month corrected‑age appointment present study details to parents and provide a written synopsis; at the 4‑month corrected‑age follow‑up appointment obtain written informed consent; record that parents may withdraw at any time without explanation and that infants will be withdrawn if health care is discontinued or adverse events occur.

steps.title: Schedule longitudinal assessment visits
steps.instruction: Arrange four assessment visits at corrected ages 4, 6, 9 and 12 months; at 6‑ and 9‑month visits collect only electrophysiological measurements (VEP, EDA) and routine clinical data to minimise burden; at 4‑ and 12‑month visits perform the full assessment battery.

steps.title: Collect clinical and sociodemographic data
steps.instruction: At the 4‑month visit record sociodemographic variables, administer the Bayley Scale of Infant and Toddler Development, apply the Participation Activity Inventory – Children and Youth (PAI‑CY), and perform the ophthalmological screening assessment; at 6‑ and 9‑month visits record clinical data collected by the neonatologist/physician during routine appointments.

steps.title: Prepare infant for electrophysiology recording
steps.instruction: Optimize placement of active electrodes and fit a cap to ensure accurate positioning; place the primary VEP electrode at Oz (use PO7 and PO8 if Oz signal is absent); configure the system for a single‑trial VEP assessment due to limited infant cooperation.

steps.title: Record VEP and EDA signals
steps.instruction: Present visual stimuli while recording VEP; use a single trial per stimulus; acquire EDA continuously at 500 Hz sampling rate; ensure triggers are logged for each stimulus.

steps.title: Process VEP data in MATLAB
steps.instruction: Apply a 4th‑order Butterworth band‑pass filter (2 Hz – 30 Hz); visually inspect the signal and select a stable segment with few artifacts; compute its standard deviation and set an artifact‑rejection threshold at 1.5 × SD; locate triggers and segment the signal into 700 ms epochs (100 ms pre‑stimulus, 600 ms post‑stimulus); discard epochs exceeding the threshold; average the remaining epochs to obtain the evoked‑potential waveform; apply a final Butterworth low‑pass filter at 10 Hz; measure N75, P100 and N135 amplitudes and latencies at Oz (or PO7/PO8 if needed).

substeps.instruction: Locate triggers, epoch 700 ms (‑100 ms to +600 ms)
Measure N75, P100, N135 amplitude and latency

steps.title: Process EDA data with Ledalab
steps.instruction: Down‑sample the raw EDA from 500 Hz to 100 Hz in MATLAB; convert the signal to microsiemens (µS); apply a 50‑point moving‑average filter; import both trigger and EDA files into Ledalab®; perform continuous deconvolution to separate tonic and phasic components; define a skin‑conductance‑response (SCR) window of 1 – 4 s with a minimum amplitude of 0.01 µS; extract for each SCR the number, latency (s), amplitude (µS), phasic driver (µS), area (µS²) and average tonic component (µS).

substeps.instruction: Set SCR window 1‑4 s, amplitude ≥0.01 µS
Extract number, latency, amplitude, phasic driver, area, tonic average

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Use SPSS version 30; conduct a mixed‑design repeated‑measures ANOVA with time (4, 6, 9, 12 months) as within‑subjects factor and group (preterm vs. full‑term) as between‑subjects factor; test normality, sphericity (Mauchly) and homogeneity of variances (Levene); apply Greenhouse–Geisser correction if sphericity is violated; perform Bonferroni‑adjusted post‑hoc pairwise comparisons; run exploratory multiple linear regression models to assess effects of clinical (gestational age, APGAR, birth weight) and socio‑demographic (mother age, parental education) variables on outcomes (Bayley motor scores, VEP latency/amplitude, EDA parameters) using change scores between first and fourth assessments; check model assumptions and multicollinearity (VIF); consider results significant at two‑sided p < 0.05.
